C.A. Das vs The Controller on 11 September, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49831065/
2  Dated, this the 26th day of September, 2013  JUDGMENT

The petitioner is aggrieved of the course and proceedings pursued by the respondents 2 and 3,
whereby two weighing machines belonging to the petitioner were simply seized by them on 07.09.2013 leaving the petitioner in dark.

The case of the petitioner is that the seizure was effected without offering any explanation or reasons, but for as a measure of highhanded act on the part of the respondents, which is turn is under challenge in this writ petition.

2. Today when the matter came up for consideration, the learned counsel for the petitioner points out that after filing writ petition, the petitioner has been served with show-cause notice bearing No.
266 of 2013 dated 11.09.2013, though it was served to the petitioner only on 19.09.2013, raising various allegations and infringement of the statutory provision.
A copy of said show-cause notice also placed for consideration of this Court.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is absolutely no merit or bonafide in the show-cause notice and that petitioner has already filed a detailed explanation/reply before the respondents.

3. It is seen from the show-cause notice that weighing machines seized from the petitioner have already produced before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Thiruvananthapuram in CMP. No. 6286 of 2013.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Thiruvananthapuram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. In the above circumstances, this Court finds that appropriate remedy of the petitioner is to pursue the matter before the concerned respondent with regard to the allegations levelled in the show-cause notice and also to approach the concerned Court by filing necessary petition to get interim custody of the weighing machines, to be dealt with in accordance with law.
It is also made clear that the contentions put forward by the petitioner both factual and legal are left open.
The Writ Petition is disposed of.

Sd/-
P. R. RAMACHANDRA MENON, (JUDGE) kmd C.A. Das vs The Controller on 11 September, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49831065/
